PullRequest.Title: Classify returned language model tool errors in telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
`languageModelToolInvoked` currently reports `success` whenever a tool invocation resolves, even when the returned `IToolResult` carries `toolResultError`.

This classifies such resolved error results as `error`, matching the result that reaches the model and UI.

Content-encoded domain outcomes remain intentionally unchanged. For example, a tool returning `{"status":"cancelled"}` without `toolResultError` still appears as generic `success` because this layer cannot safely infer tool-specific semantics from content.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `languageModelToolsService.test.ts`: 140 passing

Extracted from #337030 so the cross-cutting tool telemetry behavior can be reviewed independently.

Scenarios.Scenario: A chat or agent-host tool invocation resolves with a non-empty toolResultError and returns its result to the model/UI.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool implementation and post-execution handling complete before the existing languageModelToolInvoked telemetry call and result return. The diff adds only an O(1) read of the already-materialized toolResultError field while constructing that existing event; it adds no await or new work boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the selected built-in or extension-contributed tool; individual implementations may transitively perform IPC, filesystem, subprocess, or network work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one implementation invocation per invokeTool call; aggregate concurrency remains whatever callers already schedule.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same tool implementation was invoked once and awaited before telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the dominant critical-path operation, but its invocation count, inputs, and scheduling are unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the existing languageModelToolInvoked telemetry event after tool completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One telemetry event per resolved invocation, including returned error results; no additional event is emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same event with the same fields and cardinality was emitted, with result set to success.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing non-awaited telemetry API call remains immediately before returning the result. The diff changes only result from success to error for this case.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Carry an extension-host-originated invocation into the service and serialize the result back to the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inbound and one result IPC exchange per extension-host invocation; unchanged by the telemetry classification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same invocation and result IPC occurred; toolResultError was already included in the returned result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The service invocation must complete before the result is returned over IPC, but the added property read does not alter payload size or IPC count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the number of tool completions, but the incremental work is one truthiness check per completion, independent of result content size, tool count, or session history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No limiter or scheduling behavior changes. Concurrent tool calls continue to produce one independent existing telemetry emission each on completion.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read, populated, invalidated, or bypassed by the change; cold and warm behavior are identical.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed expression reads a string-or-boolean field already present on the in-memory result and substitutes one short enum-like telemetry value for another.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual tools can have widely varying boundary costs, but those costs and their frequency are unchanged; the incremental classification cost is negligible and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change corrects telemetry classification without adding serialization, fan-out, blocking work, or retained memory.

Scenarios.Scenario: A tool invocation resolves normally without toolResultError.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing tool implementation and post-execution flow, the changed expression performs one missing-property read and emits the same success telemetry event before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One invocation per invokeTool call, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited and potentially dominant, but unaffected by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing event per resolved invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new event or await; the resulting telemetry payload remains the same for successful results.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time property check per successful tool completion; no dependence on content array length or metadata size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged; the expression neither starts work nor serializes concurrent invocations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caches are involved or changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both branches and the surrounding telemetry call are directly visible in the changed hunk and call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed mechanism; object property access is bounded and does not inspect the error string or content.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Successful invocations retain the same telemetry value, boundary cardinality, and critical path.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced normal and returned-error tool completions through built-in/extension invocation, agent-host usage, result IPC, and telemetry. The sole production change is a constant-time truthiness check on an existing result field used to choose an existing telemetry enum value. No performance finding or performance-regression fix was identified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
